## Cancún and Belize in 11 days: who will enjoy this two-country combination?

[Cancún](/mexico/place/cancun/) and [Belize](/belize/) in one trip suit travellers who want to combine **Mayan history, Caribbean beach relaxation and snorkelling over a coral reef**. In the first part, Ada Tours organises excursions around the Yucatán Peninsula and leaves several free days for beach time. The second part includes a flight to Belize, accommodation on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/) and marine excursions.

The programme lasts 11 days and 10 nights. Overnight stays are allocated as follows: **6 in Cancún, 3 on Ambergris Caye and 1 in Belize City**. This is a significant difference from more intensive archaeological itineraries around Central America: travellers have time to relax in one resort area before the Belize section begins.

## Yucatán archaeology: Chichén Itzá, Tulum and Cobá

On day 2, an excursion to [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) is scheduled, followed by a swim in [Ik Kil Cenote](/mexico/place/ik-kil-cenote/). Chichén Itzá is among the most important centres of Yucatán history; UNESCO highlights the site's Mayan architectural traditions and the influence of Central Mexico. The Pyramid of Kukulcán conveys the scale of the ancient city, while the cenote adds variety after exploring the monuments.

The following day is devoted to [Tulum](/mexico/place/tulum/) and [Cobá](/mexico/place/coba/). Tulum's setting on a coastal cliff is unusual: its ancient port and fortifications stand directly above the Caribbean Sea. Cobá, by contrast, introduces the history of inland settlements, ancient roads and architectural complexes. The original programme mentions climbing the Nohoch Mul pyramid; access to structures and current visiting rules must be confirmed for the actual dates because archaeological-zone regulations may change.

Three free days in Cancún then follow. You can spend them by the sea or optionally join a group excursion to [Xel-Há Park](/mexico/place/xel-ha-park/), which is paid for separately. A free beach day and an optional paid excursion are alternative uses of the time, not two guaranteed activities on the same day.

## The Belize section: flight, water taxi and island

On day 7, the programme specifies a transfer to Cancún airport and a flight to Belize. After arrival in [Belize City](/belize/place/belize-city/), travellers transfer to the port, board a shared water taxi and travel to San Pedro on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). The sea crossing takes about an hour and a half. This is a full travel day involving a flight, road transfer and boat; additional activities should be planned with possible delays in mind.

The island introduces the marine environment. The programme includes an excursion to [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/) and the Shark Ray Alley area, where swimming near nurse sharks is expected. The following day focuses on snorkelling around Ambergris Caye. Fish, rays, turtles and corals can be observed in these waters, although actual wildlife sightings and conditions for going out to sea depend on the weather.

**Snorkelling is not the same as scuba diving.** Swimming with a mask and snorkel and undertaking underwater dives involve different formats, requirements and restrictions. This itinerary includes snorkelling, so certified diving excursions or included scuba equipment should not be assumed.

On day 10, an optional group sightseeing flight over [the Great Blue Hole](/belize/place/great-blue-hole/) can be added. It has a separate price and is not included among the standard excursions. After returning from the island, travellers transfer to a Belize City hotel; the following day brings a city tour and the flight home.

## How time is spent in Mexico and Belize

| Yucatán | Belize |
|---|---|
| Chichén Itzá, Tulum, Cobá | Hol Chan and Ambergris Caye |
| Cenote and Cancún beaches | Reef snorkelling |
| Russian-speaking guide | English-speaking guide |
| Road journeys | Boats and sea excursions |

When comparing trips, remember that beach relaxation occupies a substantial part of the Mexican section. If you want **more ancient cities and active excursions, with fewer resort breaks**, consider another itinerary, [“Wonders of Guatemala and Belize”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-wonders/), which includes [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) and Actun Tunichil Muknal Cave.

## What is included, and which languages do the guides speak?

The package includes standard rooms in 4-star hotels, transfers with a driver, entrance tickets, **a Russian-speaking guide for excursions in Cancún** and **an English-speaking guide in Belize**. The one-way **Cancún–Belize flight** and round-trip shared water taxi between Belize City and San Pedro are also included.

Thus, the expression “with a Russian-speaking guide” refers to the Mexican excursions; **it does not promise Russian-language guiding in Belize**. Additional meals, optional excursions and medical services are paid for separately. Xel-Há and the sightseeing flight over the Blue Hole are mentioned as paid options. Ada Tours may adjust hotels and the sequence of excursions while maintaining the accommodation category and programme content.

The trip begins in Cancún and finishes in Belize City. Flight planning must account for different arrival and departure airports, possible connections and sufficient time for the water transfer. Visa and transit requirements must be checked separately **for each traveller's citizenship against the current rules** of Mexico, Belize and any intermediate countries.

## Preparing for the journey

Archaeological excursions call for comfortable footwear, sun protection and readiness to spend several hours at outdoor sites. For swimming in the cenote and boat trips, bring clothing that can be changed and dried quickly. Marine activities around Ambergris Caye should be planned according to the forecast, local guides' instructions and your swimming ability.

The main organisational issue is combining scheduled excursions with enough free time. On this tour, the solution is to split the journey into two stages: Yucatán includes beach breaks between Mayan sites, while Belize focuses on the reef and marine life.

## Frequently asked questions about the Cancún–Belize tour

### How many days can be spent on the beach without excursions?

Three free days are provided in Cancún after visiting the archaeological sites. You can leave them for relaxation or use one for the optional Xel-Há excursion.

### Does a Russian-speaking guide accompany the whole journey?

No. A Russian-speaking guide leads the excursions in Cancún, while an English-speaking guide works during the Belize section. Consider this before booking.

### Is diving in the Great Blue Hole included?

No. The programme includes snorkelling around Ambergris Caye and an optional sightseeing flight over the Blue Hole. No separate scuba-diving programme is specified.

### Must I buy the Cancún–Belize flight separately?

No. The one-way flight between these countries is listed among the included services. The international journey to the starting point and return home require separate arrangements.

## Five Central American countries in 19 days: from Tikal to Arenal

Over **19 days and 18 nights**, you will travel through five countries: **Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica**. The itinerary combines cities and Mayan archaeological sites with volcanic regions, the Caribbean coast and tropical national parks. This trip is for travellers who want to explore the region in sequence rather than limit themselves to a single country and a handful of famous resorts.

The journey begins in Guatemala City and Antigua, passes through Tikal and Honduras to El Salvador and Nicaragua, and concludes in Costa Rica. Readiness for lengthy transfers and international border crossings is important: the programme is packed with excursions on almost every day.

## What makes each country different?

| Country | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Guatemala | Antigua, Atitlán, Tikal |
| Honduras | Copán and Mayan culture |
| El Salvador | San Andrés, Joya de Cerén |
| Nicaragua | León, Masaya, Granada |
| Costa Rica | Monteverde, Arenal, Poás |

In Guatemala, the itinerary begins in [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), a colonial city surrounded by volcanoes. You then visit Pacaya Volcano and [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), where the programme introduces the communities of San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán. Chichicastenango is known for its local market and traditional crafts.

Day 6 is devoted to [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). Tikal National Park is UNESCO-listed for both cultural and natural significance. The temples stand in tropical forest, so walking through the archaeological complex gives you a sense of both the Mayan political centre and the natural surroundings of Petén.

## Why are Quiriguá and Copán included?

The next Guatemalan section travels through Río Dulce and Livingston to [Quiriguá](/guatemala/place/quirigua/). The Quiriguá archaeological complex is known for carved stelae depicting rulers and bearing hieroglyphic inscriptions. UNESCO highlights the preservation of these monuments and the value of the inscriptions for understanding the Classic Maya period.

The route then crosses into Honduras and leads to [Copán Ruinas](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/). Travellers can compare several archaeological cities belonging to one civilisation, each with its own history, architecture and epigraphy. Copán is especially celebrated for sculpture and the Hieroglyphic Stairway.

Having three different sites in a single programme means that sightseeing time is allocated to each, but there are no separate multi-day archaeological expeditions. The route is designed to offer a broad introduction to Central American heritage.

## El Salvador and Nicaragua: settlements and colonial cities

In El Salvador, the programme includes San Salvador and the archaeological areas of San Andrés and [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/). Joya de Cerén is a UNESCO World Heritage site preserving traces of everyday life in a pre-Columbian settlement buried beneath volcanic deposits. Unlike the temple centres of Tikal and Copán, it provides unusual insight into ordinary housing and daily activities.

From there, the journey continues via La Unión into Nicaragua. León, Managua, Granada and the Masaya area are all included. In [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), the historic city plan is of interest, while the volcanic area provides a geological contrast with the Guatemalan stage.

Access to active volcanoes and particular viewpoints depends on safety regulations. If a park restricts visits because of volcanic activity or gas emissions, the actual programme must comply with those restrictions.

## Costa Rica: from the Pacific coast to cloud forests

The final stage starts on Costa Rica's coast and then moves to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Cloud forests are known for humid conditions and a diversity of plants, birds and other animals. Silence, season and weather matter for wildlife watching; a sighting of a particular rare species cannot be promised on every outing.

The route continues to [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), Poás Volcano and La Paz Waterfalls. After temples and old cities, this introduces another side of Central America: lakes, forests, volcanic formations and wetlands.

## Price and included services

The trip costs **from $10,780**. The package includes hotel accommodation, transfers, a Russian-speaking guide, excursions, accommodation taxes and **a domestic flight from Guatemala City to Flores**. Meals are provided on particular days according to the itinerary, so three meals a day must not be assumed throughout all 19 days.

**Optional activities, airport fees and personal expenses** are listed as payable separately. Other flights cannot be assumed included merely because the Flores flight is: the commercial terms explicitly identify that particular domestic segment.

When budgeting for the complete journey, account not only for the package price, but also international arrival in Guatemala and departure from Costa Rica, potential visa and transit formalities, and personal spending during free periods.

## Preparing for travel through five countries

This itinerary involves repeated document checks and transfers between countries. Participants should confirm permitted stays, visa and proof-of-onward-travel requirements for their nationality in advance. Conditions at individual borders may differ by entry method, so one country's general rules cannot be applied to the entire region.

For archaeological sites, lightweight long clothing, a hat, water and closed-toe shoes are useful; bring a waterproof layer for cloud forests and something warm for volcanic highlands. Count long transfer days as part of the journey and allow time for road delays.

## Comparing the itinerary with a route through Panama

The [13-day Panama–Costa Rica–Nicaragua tour](/multi-country/tour/panama-costa-rica-nicaragua/) focuses more on nature parks, the coast and the Panama Canal. The 19-day programme adds Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador, making it particularly attractive for Mayan archaeology and the history of colonial cities.

Choose by your principal motivation: five countries and extensive Mayan heritage, or a shorter journey with more emphasis on nature. Both routes involve active sightseeing and several changes of hotel.

## Frequently asked questions about the five countries

### Which countries are included in the 19-day itinerary?

Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica, in that order. Arrival is planned in Guatemala, with the return flight from San José.

### How is Tikal different from Joya de Cerén?

Tikal is famous for its temple complexes, palaces and Mayan cultural heritage, while Joya de Cerén preserves archaeological evidence of everyday life in a pre-Columbian village.

### Is a domestic flight included?

Yes. The included-services list specifically names the **Guatemala City–Flores** flight. Other flights and fees are governed by the itinerary's terms.

### Are all excursions conducted in Russian?

A Russian-speaking guide is specified in the main included-services list. For individual days and transport sections, guiding arrangements are determined by the programme.

## Central America: a journey through 8 countries in 26 days

The extended itinerary from Mexico City to Panama City is designed for travellers who want to explore archaeological monuments, colonial towns and natural areas of Central America in sequence. Instead of several separate holidays, the programme brings together **Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama**.

Over 26 days, the landscapes change dramatically: first Mayan temples and cities, then volcanoes and lakes, cloud forests, tropical rivers and the Panama Canal. The price of this variety is frequent transfers, border formalities and physical exertion on some nature excursions. The tour is most suitable for people prepared for active travel and ready to coordinate complicated logistics in advance.

## All eight countries in order

| Days | Country and main programme |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | Mexico: Mexico City, Teotihuacán, Mérida, Chichén Itzá |
| 6–7 | Belize: San Ignacio, Caracol, natural pools |
| 8–11 | Guatemala: Tikal, Antigua, Pacaya, Atitlán |
| 12–13 | Honduras: Copán |
| 14 | El Salvador: capital and archaeological sites |
| 15–18 | Nicaragua: Granada, León, Estelí; transfer to Costa Rica |
| 19–24 | Costa Rica: Monteverde, Arenal, Tortuguero |
| 25–26 | Panama: Chagres, Emberá, canal and departure |

The table shows the sequence of principal stops. A travel day may involve more than one country, and transfer duration depends on agreed flights and actual border operations.

## Archaeology: from Yucatán to Copán

The first stage begins in Mexico City and Teotihuacán. The route then continues through Mérida and [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/), one of the major Mayan complexes of Yucatán. UNESCO notes the combination of Mayan and Toltec traditions in its surviving stone buildings.

In Belize, the itinerary includes Caracol and natural areas around San Ignacio. Travellers then reach [Tikal in Guatemala](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), with great temple structures standing amid tropical forest. In [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), colonial architecture and textile workshops add another dimension to the archaeological journey.

In Honduras, the principal site is Copán, renowned for its stelae and Hieroglyphic Stairway. El Salvador offers different monuments, including [Joya de Cerén](/el-salvador/place/joya-de-ceren/). This archaeological site preserves evidence of everyday life in a farming settlement buried beneath volcanic ash. The journey thus reveals not only the rulers of ancient cities but also ordinary people's lives.

## Volcanoes, forests and rivers

In Guatemala, an active nature day is dedicated to [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/). The climbing section runs at approximately 1,900–2,300 metres above sea level. This is a hiking excursion, so your experience and physical abilities should guide your decision.

In Nicaragua, the route passes through Granada, Masaya, León and Estelí. Cities, crafts and volcanic geography make up the core experiences here. In Estelí, the itinerary specifically includes cigar production and murals.

Costa Rica offers a different natural setting. Around Monteverde, the programme includes cloud forest; this is followed by El Tigre Waterfalls and the Arenal area. El Tigre involves approximately three hours of walking on a moderately to highly challenging trail, plus a horseback section. You should be physically prepared for this outing.

The journey then reaches [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), where a sunrise boat excursion through the canals is included. Bird and animal encounters depend on nature, timing and weather; participation does not guarantee a particular sighting.

## The finale: Panama and the canal

In Panama, the itinerary includes an encounter with the Emberá community in the Chagres area and an introduction to the river environment. A traditional lunch in Tusipono is specifically included on that day's programme. Visits to [Miraflores Locks](/panama/place/miraflores-locks/) on the Panama Canal and sightseeing in Panama City follow.

The final day combines an excursion with departure, so its timing must be coordinated with the international flight. An early departure may require rescheduling part of the last day's programme.

## Services, flights and important hotel questions

Included services list transfers, bed-and-breakfast accommodation, excursions with **English-speaking guides**, entrance tickets according to the programme, a light snack at El Tigre and a traditional lunch in Tusipono. Other meals and drinks, personal expenses, tips and laundry are charged separately.

The **flight inclusions** require particular attention. The itinerary involves flights between several cities, but international and domestic flights appear on the exclusion list. By contrast, one line of the hotel quotation mentions flights. Until the ticket package is confirmed, flights should not be considered a paid-for part of the package.

There is also a discrepancy in accommodation allocation: the heading specifies **26 days and 25 nights**, but the sum of nights in the hotel table is 26. Individual hotel rows need to be reconciled with the daily itinerary. The final price and departure dates have not yet been confirmed. All these details must be agreed before booking.

For a different format, compare shorter programmes for two countries, such as [Guatemala–Belize in 12 days](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/). They involve fewer transfers and more time at particular sites. The eight-country tour makes sense when exploring the full region in sequence is the main purpose.

## Frequently asked questions about the Central American tour

### Are all eight countries included?

Yes. The programme travels through Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama, in that order.

### What language do the guides speak?

The included excursions have English-speaking guides. A Russian-speaking guide for the entire itinerary has not been confirmed.

### How physically demanding is the tour?

Most city excursions are conventional sightseeing trips, but Pacaya and El Tigre involve substantial walking. Assess your readiness for hiking and humid conditions on nature days.

### Are all flights included?

This cannot yet be confirmed. International and domestic flights are named on the exclusion list, while a separate line of the quotation needs clarification. The final transport package is agreed separately.

### How many hotel nights are provided?

The heading states 25 nights, but the current hotel table totals a different number. The exact allocation must be agreed before payment.

## Chile, Argentina and Brazil in 15 days: from Patagonia to Rio

The journey begins in Chile, continues through Argentina and concludes in Brazil. Over **15 days and 14 nights**, you will visit Santiago, Chilean Patagonia, Perito Moreno Glacier, Buenos Aires, Iguazu Falls and Rio de Janeiro.

The main attraction of this sequence is the transition **from cool glacial regions to the warm ocean coast**. The last days in Rio include free time, so the journey ends at a calmer pace than the border crossings and national parks in its first half.

## Stages and transfers

| Days | Area |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Santiago |
| 3–4 | Chilean Patagonia |
| 5–6 | El Calafate, Perito Moreno |
| 7–9 | Buenos Aires |
| 10–11 | Iguazu |
| 12–15 | Rio de Janeiro |

The first flight within the itinerary takes the group from Santiago south to Chile's Punta Arenas area, followed by a road journey to Puerto Natales. Later comes an overland border crossing to El Calafate in Argentina. After Patagonia, flights are needed to Buenos Aires, Iguazu and Rio.

**Domestic flights on this tour are paid for separately.** This is an important difference from some other multi-country packages in which domestic tickets are included. Budget for every flight segment, as well as potential connections and baggage allowances.

## Santiago and Chilean Patagonia

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a tour introduces Plaza de Armas, La Moneda, Santa Lucía Hill and modern neighbourhoods. An optional excursion to the [Maipo wine valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) is offered separately if the timetable allows.

The journey then continues to [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The park excursion includes nature stops, mountain views, lakes and steppe scenery. Milodon Cave and Salto Grande are mentioned in the area. **The multi-day W Trek is not included in the mandatory programme**: this is a sightseeing visit to Patagonia.

Wind and weather at Torres del Paine may change during a single day. Stable closed-toe shoes, a waterproof jacket and a warm layer are needed for viewpoints and short walks. The park authority controls access to individual trails.

## Perito Moreno and Buenos Aires: two sides of Argentina

The group crosses into Argentina by road. The base for visiting the glacier is [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). A full sightseeing day is dedicated to [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). The principal views are from walkways looking onto the glacier's front above the lake.

After the nature section, the trip continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). A city tour of historic and modern districts and an evening tango show are included. The next day is free: guests can stay in the city or choose an optional trip to Tigre, an introduction to gaucho rural culture or a one-day excursion into Uruguay.

**Uruguay is not one of the three main countries on this journey.** Visiting Montevideo or Colonia del Sacramento is an individual optional choice, not part of the mandatory geography for everyone.

## Iguazu from both sides, then the ocean and Rio

At the falls, the main programme presents two perspectives. Trails on the Argentine side approach individual cascades; from [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) on the Brazilian side, the whole waterfall system is easier to see. Macuco Safari, a helicopter flight and the Bird Park are separately offered in the region. The availability of an option **does not mean its cost is included**.

The finale takes place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Visits include [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/), [Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/), the historic centre and a free day. You can spend the latter on the beaches or book an additional excursion without altering the mandatory route.

## Guides and included services

This tour costs **from $5,979**. The programme includes **standard-category 4-star hotels with breakfasts**, driver transfers, excursions and meals as specified. **Russian-speaking guides** are provided for city tours in Buenos Aires and Santiago. **English-speaking guides** lead the group excursions in the Puerto Natales and El Calafate areas.

International and domestic flights are paid for separately. Optional activities, meals outside those included, tips and personal expenses are also extra. Thus, the final cost depends on the flights and optional trips selected, not only on hotel rates.

## Choosing this route or another option

This tour suits travellers who want to **see Patagonia first, then conclude with the ocean and Rio**. Several days are spent in Santiago, Buenos Aires and Rio, while the nature outings in Patagonia and at Iguazu form the heart of the journey.

If the Atacama Desert or an in-depth wine programme is the priority, do not attribute these to this itinerary: Maipo is optional, and the published 15 days include no extended Atacama section. To expand the geography, compare [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/); for routes focused on nature, see [wildlife trips](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Chile–Argentina–Brazil tour

### How long is the journey?

**15 days and 14 nights.** It begins in Santiago and ends in Rio de Janeiro.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Domestic flights are charged separately from the tour price.

### Is there time for independent walks?

Yes. Free days are included in Buenos Aires and Rio, with some free time after arrival in Santiago.

### Are all excursions in Russian?

No. Russian-speaking guides are provided in Santiago and Buenos Aires; English-speaking guides are specified for group excursions in Patagonia.

## “Chile & Argentina Deluxe”: Patagonia, Iguazu and Buenos Aires in 14 days

Chile and Argentina appear in the tour's name, but **Brazil is also part of its main itinerary**. Over 14 days and 13 nights, travellers see Chile's Pacific coast, the granite peaks of Torres del Paine, Perito Moreno Glacier, Bariloche's lakes, both sides of Iguazu Falls and the historic districts of Buenos Aires. The journey combines successive flights and road transfers for those who want to discover contrasts among South American regions.

The main question when choosing such a trip is whether you are willing to change hotels and climates several times for the sake of extensive geography. A separate holiday would be better for a long stay in one national park. Here, variety in landscapes and activities takes priority.

## The first days: Santiago, the Pacific and Chilean Patagonia

The journey begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide is included; the following excursion explores [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). The stop combines a historic port, seaside districts and Pablo Neruda's La Sebastiana house museum.

A flight to Puerto Natales then takes the group to southern Chile. A full day is dedicated to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) with an English-speaking guide. The programme includes granite peaks, glacial lakes, Salto Grande Waterfall and Milodon Cave. It is a sightseeing format with vehicle stops and walks: no multi-day camping trek is included.

## Argentine Patagonia: Perito Moreno Glacier and the lakes

After Puerto Natales, an overland transfer crosses the border to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). This is the gateway to Los Glaciares National Park, where visitors explore [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). Its immense wall of ice, observation walkways and Lago Argentino offer a very different view of Patagonia from Torres del Paine.

The next stop is [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/). The itinerary includes a lake-region journey through the Limay Valley, views of Lake Traful, Villa Traful and Villa La Angostura. The “Seven Lakes” trip occupies a full day because of the long route and numerous stops.

When comparing stages, consider the total length of each day, not only the scheduled start of an excursion. Flights and changes of city also require time for check-in, travel and accommodation.

## Why the third country, Brazil, matters

On day 10, a flight from Bariloche to the Iguazu region via Buenos Aires is planned. After glaciers and Patagonia's cool lakes, travellers enter subtropical forest. On the Brazilian side at [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the programme includes the waterfalls, Macuco Safari, Bird Park and a helicopter excursion. The following day focuses on the Argentine side via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

The Brazilian panoramas reveal the extended front of the cascades, while Argentine walkways bring visitors closer to the water and viewpoints. Each side has its own access requirements, and eligibility to enter both countries should be checked for each traveller's citizenship.

The final stage is [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): a sightseeing tour of historic neighbourhoods and an evening tango show with dinner.

## Included services and additional expenses

The package covers accommodation in the listed hotels or hotels of comparable category, guides, excursions and transfers along the route, tickets and meals as specified. The guiding language varies: some days have Russian-speaking guides, others English-speaking guides.

**International and domestic flights are paid for separately.** The estimated cost of domestic flights starts at $850 per person. Optional excursions, tips, drinks and meals beyond those included are also extra. When calculating the complete budget, compare the exact included-services list rather than only the tour's initial price.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour

### How many countries are visited?

The main countries are Chile, Argentina and Brazil. The name “Chile & Argentina Deluxe” reflects the primary geography, but the Brazilian side of Iguazu is included too.

### Are there long hiking trips?

This is a sightseeing itinerary with walks, road transfers and flights. There is no multi-day hike with overnight stays outside hotels.

### Are domestic flights already paid for?

No. They appear among the excluded services, so the airfare must be added when calculating the budget.

### Can we see both sides of Iguazu Falls?

Yes. Separate parts of the programme are dedicated to the Brazilian and Argentine sides. The precise order of visits may change while preserving the planned excursions.
